html:
SMTO-LLM-0066 — The model server didn't start

GUID: 5b20b89c-7612-56cf-88dc-f547e4380653
Slug: local-ai-start-failed
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: local_ai

What happened

  • SMTO tried to start the model server, but it couldn't be launched, it stopped soon after starting, or the Gateway was about to restart. It may have run briefly first.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to show the logs for this Local AI runtime on that Gateway, the helper program SMTO uses on that computer. The error alone does not establish why it stopped; the model server's own messages usually do, such as running out of graphics card memory. If it never launched, there may be no log.
  2. Ask SMTO to show this runtime's status and make sure it says exited or stopped. Starting again while the earlier attempt is still alive could create a second copy.
  3. Fix what the log points to, for example lower ctx_size or gpu_memory_utilization in the profile's extra options in Parameter Store, then select Save. Smaller memory settings often let a model fit on the available graphics card.
  4. Start the model server again in a new message that names the profile with @; if the Gateway was restarting, wait for that first. A new message uses your saved fix, and a restarting Gateway refuses new starts.

What success looks like

  • The model server's status shows ready and stays that way.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and the log text, and send them to the person who manages that Gateway. Don't stop programs on that computer that SMTO didn't start.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Local AI start failed: the Gateway had a restart pending, process creation raised an error, or the spawned process exited before its health check succeeded; the receipt's runtime record shows whether a process was created.

What this means

  • Startup was rejected while restart was pending, process creation failed, or a spawned process exited before readiness; the receipt distinguishes whether a process was created. Local AI management belongs to the selected Gateway and accepted profile. Starting a runtime does not activate it for the controller; recorded execution and unknown-effect facts determine whether reconciliation is required.

Why this can happen

  • Startup was rejected while restart was pending, process creation failed, or a spawned process exited before readiness; the receipt distinguishes whether a process was created.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare executed/process state and the existing runtime's bounded log; distinguish spawn failure from an immediate process exit.

How to fix it

  • Read the runtime record and logs (local_ai.runtime and local_ai.logs for the runtime_id in the receipt) for the provider's own error, such as GPU out-of-memory, an unsupported option or an unreadable model. Fix the profile or host, confirm the runtime is exited or stopped, wait out any pending Gateway restart, then start again.
  • Repair the concrete launch/log error and reconcile the existing runtime before requesting another start.

Retry and execution caution

  • Only after exact state reconciliation.

How to verify the fix

  • The same accepted profile reaches ready state with a live owned process.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations or stop externally owned processes.

Technical notes

  • Local AI management belongs to the selected Gateway and accepted profile. Starting a runtime does not activate it for the controller; recorded execution and unknown-effect facts determine whether reconciliation is required.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
